learn.intro: Hi! Today is lesson 12: **CSS variables and animations**. We'll learn to change the color of the whole site with one line and bring buttons and cards to life. Let's go!

slides.text: In our project the same purple color is used in **15 places**. If the designer asks for another color, you'd have to edit all 15. CSS variables solve this with **one edit**.
A variable is declared at the very top of `style.css`, inside `:root`:
`:root` is the whole document (`html`). A variable declared here works **everywhere on the page**.
A variable name always starts with two dashes: --main-color.

check.prompt: A variable from :root only works inside body.
check.explain: :root is the whole document, so the variable works on the whole page.
A CSS variable name starts with --.

slides.text: First let's count: in VS Code press **Ctrl+F** and search for `#7c3aed`. See how many places?
Instead of the color we write `var(--main-color)`:
Now we change the color **in one place** — and all buttons change at once:
The most common mistakes: forgetting -- or writing var(main-color). If it doesn't work — check the value in DevTools, in the Computed tab.

check.explain: A variable's value is taken with var().

options: var must be in capital letters

slides.text: Without smoothness, the color on hover changes **abruptly**, in a jump:
Add `transition` — and the state change becomes **smooth**:
Try changing `0.3s` to `0.1s` and to `1s` — feel the difference yourself.

check.explain: transition stretches the change over time so it isn't abrupt.

check.prompt: transition: background-color 1s ease — the change is slower than with 0.3s.

slides.text: Let's make a button that «breathes»:
`0%`, `50%`, `100%` are the **stages** of the animation. `2s` is the duration, `infinite` means repeat forever.
Don't put an endless animation on every button — motion is distracting. Show it, then remove it.

check.prompt: What does infinite mean in animation: breathe 2s infinite?

slides.text: The three main transform functions:
`scale` — **enlarge**, `translate` — **move**, `rotate` — **turn**.
All three change how the element looks, not its place on the page.

check.prompt: Match the function and the action

check.explain: rotate means turn, deg means degrees.

slides.text: Task: add a hover animation to all `.card` cards:
Write transition in the main .card rule, not in :hover. Otherwise there's no smoothness when the mouse leaves.

Homework: move hardcoded values into variables in `:root` — the colors `#7c3aed`, `#14141f`, `#a1a1b5`, `#ffffff` and the 16px, 24px spacing. Use meaningful names: `--main-color`, `--card-bg`, `--gap`.

check.prompt: Where is the right place to write transition for a card?
check.explain: In the main rule — then it's smooth both on hover and when the mouse leaves.

questions.prompt: A CSS variable name starts with two dashes --.
Where do you declare variables so they work on the whole page?

questions.explain: A variable's value is taken with var().

questions.prompt: What color will the button be?
If you change --main-color in :root, every element with var(--main-color) changes.
questions.explain: That's the point of variables: one edit — it changes everywhere.

options: You can't use var in color

questions.explain: Without transition the change is abrupt.

questions.prompt: Build a smooth background change over 0.3 seconds
Where do you write transition so it's smooth even when the mouse leaves?
questions.explain: If it's only in :hover, the card snaps back abruptly when the mouse leaves.

questions.prompt: Match the transform and what it does
transform changes an element's place, and neighboring elements move.
questions.explain: transform only changes how the element looks, not its place.

questions.prompt: What do 0%, 50%, 100% mean in this animation?
questions.explain: These are moments of the animation: start, middle, end.

questions.prompt: Which word in animation: breathe 2s infinite; makes the animation endless?
How do you attach the breathe animation to a button for 2 seconds?
questions.explain: An animation from @keyframes is attached with the animation property.
